methodological_rigor.justification: Well-designed discovery-and-validation approach with 8 independent cohorts totaling >2000 patients. Early-stage HCC cohorts (D1, V2) defined clinical response by pathological criteria (≥50% tumor necrosis). Comprehensive immunological characterization with complementary techniques (scRNA-seq, BCR-seq, spatial transcriptomics, seromics, flow cytometry, ELISpot). Statistical methods appropriate (Wilcoxon tests, Dirichlet regression, FDR correction). IRB approvals documented. Limitations acknowledged regarding single-cell sample biasing and early-stage disease focus.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Discovery and validation cohorts provide solid evidence. Identifies clinically actionable IgG1 plasma cell signature across multiple immunotherapy modalities (anti-PD-1, anti-CTLA-4, anti-VEGF-A) and tumor types (HCC, melanoma, NSCLC). Serological markers (anti-NY-ESO-1 IgG1) are potentially biomarkers for patient selection and response prediction. Survival analyses validate association with improved outcomes in immunotherapy (but not chemotherapy) contexts, suggesting mechanistic specificity.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods for each cohort and analytical approach (ELISA, ELISpot, scRNA-seq, BCR-seq, spatial transcriptomics, seromics). Data availability documented: some cohorts from GEO, dbGaP; others from original authors. Reporting follows observational study structure. Nature Portfolio reporting summary mentioned. Code availability not explicitly stated but methods sufficiently detailed for reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel characterization of humoral immunity in ICB response, complementing extensive prior work on T cells. First demonstration of clonally expanded IgG1+ plasma cells enriched in responders across multiple cohorts. Identifies specific cancer-testis antigens (NY-ESO-1, PRAME, GAGE7) as targets of antitumor IgG1. Links B cell clonal tracking to clinical outcome prediction, a relatively underexplored avenue in immuno-oncology.

writing_presentation.justification: Exceptionally clear manuscript with logical flow: discovery in HCC → validation in 8 independent cohorts → mechanistic insights via cell-cell interaction and trajectory analysis. Figure quality excellent (UMAP, volcano plots, spatial analysis clearly annotated). Comprehensive figure legends with statistical details. Methods section thorough with appropriate detail for reproducibility. Discussion contextualizes findings within ICB biology.

key_strengths: Rigorous discovery-and-validation design across 8 independent cohorts encompassing >2000 patients with multiple immunotherapy modalities (PD-1, CTLA-4, VEGF-A), demonstrating broad generalizability

Comprehensive multi-modal immunological characterization: scRNA-seq, BCR-seq with clonal tracking, spatial transcriptomics, multiplex IHC, seromics against ~21,000 proteins, and functional ELISpot assays linking antibodies to CD8+ T cell responses

Identifies clinically actionable serological biomarkers (IgG1 antibodies to NY-ESO-1, MAGE-A, GAGE7, PRAME) associated with response; high IGHG1 expression linked to improved OS in immunotherapy trials but not chemotherapy, suggesting mechanistic specificity
Novel evidence for humoral-cellular immune axis in ICB response: IgG1 plasma cells trafficking between tumor and draining lymph node, supporting antigen-driven clonal expansion
High-quality visualizations and exceptionally clear presentation of complex multi-dimensional data
key_concerns: Observational discovery cohort (n=38 with responder bias: ≥50% pathologic necrosis) limits causal inference; early-stage HCC with high response rates may not generalize to metastatic/refractory disease
Single-cell cohorts small and potentially biased toward immunologically active regions; spatial transcriptomics from only 7 samples with 4 responders limits representation
Serological marker validation limited to one HCC cohort (n=8 responders, 8 non-responders) with ELISpot; prospective validation in larger cohorts recommended before clinical deployment
Biomarker cutoffs for seropositivity (titer >100) determined empirically without external validation; utility for clinical prognostication remains theoretical
Cannot definitively establish causality: elevated baseline IgG1 in some responders could reflect response prediction rather than causal contribution to immunity
chief_reviewer.rationale: Landmark manuscript establishing new biological paradigm linking humoral immunity to ICB response with strong multi-cohort validation, clinically relevant biomarkers, and mechanistic insights. Appropriate for Tier 1 journals with very minor revisions focusing on prospective validation and clinical translation pathways.
